Well first and foremost this is how I level up.

The thing with gw is that you don't really need to grind any particular event or anything to level up, even roaming to other places and doing your personal storyline will eventually get you to level 80. I personally prefer if ppl go on about this route by exploring all the maps and finishing their personal storyline before going in to pvp or wvw or even dungeons, because if you do all the maps and finish your personal storyline you will know about your class very well. I know you hate hearts and etc but even exploring gives you exp and finishing your daily will give you that write of experience thing. But i mean if you really love grinding a certain event i personally love the events in kessex hills but since you're level 40 i suggest going for dungeons now if you don't really want to explore. Another place to go is Edge of the mist (press "B" and choose Edge of the mist) its like a mini wvw where ppl zerg and you can get lots of karma and exp, a lot of veteran players and new players come here to level up to lvl 80 but again I'm against this unless you're leveling your alt.

As for dungeons each dungeon is located in a different map and you will need to go to the corresponding map to enter the dungeon for example Caude manor is located in Queensdale. To find a dungeon group just press "Y" and click on the "dungeons" tab and find which dungeon you want although some dungeons have level cap like Arah you need to be lvl 80 to do the dungeon i believe. Dungeons does not scale ppl to lvl 80 instead the scale down the higher level to the corresponding level of the dungeon, i believe the lowest one is ascalonian catacomb (Correct me if I'm wrong ppl) is level 35 i believe. If you do want to do dungeons now i suggest going over to gw2 dungeons and look at which dungeon you want to do and just give it a read so you know the basics.

However i still believe in exploring until you are comfortable with your class before going into any dungeons at all.

If you need anything IGN: "Boo D Mes" just hit me up whenever I'm online.

For leveling doing Personal Story is probably the easiest thing to do and you get tons of experience, so good job keeping up with it. For other things, exploring and doing world bosses can net you good loot and XP as well.

There are "GW2 Boss Timers" available all over the Internet, I personally use this one: http://robocafaz.com/magswag/#/timer

You can copy the "Waypoint Code" and paste it into in-game chat to create a clickable waypoint link so you can fast travel easier, in time you'll start remembering where each World Boss is. You can only get loot from each World Boss once a day(resets 17UTC I believe, which is 5pm PST/8pm EST), but you can keep doing them whenever they are active for XP, you just won't get loot. Also they are only in specific areas thus will have levels based on that area, for example Shadow Behemoth is level 15 and is located in Queensdale, there is always tons of people doing World Bosses so you should never be alone fighting one.

World Boss wiki for more info: https://wiki.guildwars2.com/wiki/World_boss

Most of the World Bosses are pretty straight-forward; attack, it becomes invulnerable for X seconds until you do Y objective, then attack it again, and repeat. Some World Bosses are harder than others, like Tequatl, but most of the are simple.

If you want to level extremely fast then you can do Professions/Crafting, but they do cost a lot of Gold. I use this website for Crafting costs and guides: http://gw2crafts.net/

I don't recommend Crafting, at least for your first character.

Caligula reproached the senators and people for the criticism they had heaped on his predecessor, Tiberius - in which he himself had previously taken part. "Thereupon," writes Cassius Dio, "he took up separately the case of each man who had lost his life, and tried to show, as people thought at least, that the senators had been responsible for the death of most of them, some by accusing them, others by testifying against them, and all by their votes of condemnation. The evidence of this, purporting to be derived from those very documents that he once declared he had burned, he caused to be read to them by the imperial freemen." And he added, "If Tiberius really did do wrong, you ought not, by Jupiter, to have honored him while he lived, and then, after repeatedly saying and voting what you did, turn about now. But it was not Tiberius alone that you treated in a fickle manner; Sejanus also you first puffed up with conceit and spoiled, then put him to death. Therefore I, too, ought not to expect any decent treatment from you" (Dio 59.16.2-4)"

Source:

Winterling, Aloys, and Deborah Lucas Schneider. "The Conflicts Escalate." Caligula: A Biography. Berkeley: U of California, 2011. 96, 97. Print.

I've been looking for ideas and discussion on carrying a full sized pistol (Taurus PT92) at appendix but every forum I come across is a bunch of fucking fat guys talking about their fupas and how they can't carry comfortably there. I'm currently with an OWB until my IWB arrives which since it's an Alien Gear cloak tuck 3.0, could be close to a month. Carrying at 4-5 often leaves a noticeable bulge with a gun this size, but carrying at 12, as awkward as going to the bathroom can be, conceals a service sized pistol pretty well. I was just curious how other thin people carry.
Who here is a concealed carrier?

I carry there on occasion, but illegally since there's no ATC in Canada. It sorta sticks out a little but no one has ever noticed. Normally I only take it out when I go camping deep in the woods and then I use a shoulder holster.

Appendix is definitely the way to go. I carry a little to the strong side of the front, so the the barrel rides towards the intersection of hip and thigh. That way the magazine on the opposite side is clear as well.

Good for you on carrying a full sized. I like the 'concealed' part of CC best, so I carry a glock 43. No way in hell is that ever leaving a profile. I always seem to silhouette when I've got a bigger gun.

Fortunately I live in an open carry state as well so printing is more of a self conscious issue because there is never any telling who might flip out over it. I do show from time to time but usually it's nothing too obvious, and that's with a fabric OWB so hopefully things will go easier with an IWB.
I love my G 43. Sits just right in the same spot you talk about.

Thats a good holster I just got the same one for my Smith and Wesson M&P 45 C I normally carry at about 3:30 4:00 position and have the clips set as high as they'll go (so the Gun rides lower in my pants) this works for me pretty well although I can't wear too tight of a shirt. that's a pretty big grip on that gun if you're having trouble with printing try adjusting the canter forward a bit as for appendix carry and middle of the back I've never had much success in those spots I always seem to print pretty bad whenever I try that. If your financial situation allows it's always nice to keep 3 guns on hand for carry small medium and large and fit a gun to what you're wearing that day I highly recommend picking up a little pocket 380 (Kel Tec PTA3/Ruger LCP) for when you're in light clothes or just really don't want anybody to know. They're cheap guns and are nice for a quick run to the store. not a day goes by I don't have the kel-tec on me but the Smith has to stay home about half the time. P.s that holster is not designed for appendix carry it will probably be too wide to fit there that particular ones Best on the hip
